browser_close.reason: The runner owns browser cleanup so it can finish writing evidence even when the model fails. Closing the browser is not part of a user task.

browser_resize.reason: Changing viewport size is a normal UI action that may reveal responsive or clipped controls without bypassing the interface.

browser_console_messages.reason: Console logs expose application internals that a normal operator cannot see and are unnecessary for completing the documented workflows.

browser_handle_dialog.reason: The simulated final submission uses a native confirmation dialog. Accepting it is separately gated by scenario authorization.

browser_evaluate.description: Evaluate a JavaScript expression on the page or an element.
browser_evaluate.reason: Arbitrary page JavaScript can read or change state without using the visible UI, defeating the purpose of the computer-use experiment.

browser_file_upload.description: Upload one or multiple local files.
browser_file_upload.reason: The target app has no upload workflow, and exposing local file paths would add unnecessary filesystem authority.

browser_drop.description: Drop local files or MIME-typed data onto an element.
browser_drop.reason: The target app has no external file or data-drop workflow; this would add filesystem and arbitrary-data input that no scenario needs.

browser_find.description: Search the current accessibility snapshot for text or a regular expression.
browser_find.reason: Searching the accessibility snapshot is still observation of the visible UI and may reduce tokens on large legacy pages.

browser_fill_form.description: Fill multiple form fields in one browser action.
browser_fill_form.reason: Several target workflows contain multi-field forms, and grouped field entry remains a visible UI interaction.

browser_press_key.reason: Keyboard interaction may be required by legacy controls or function-key-style navigation.

browser_type.description: Type text into an editable element.
browser_type.reason: Entering member numbers, nicknames, and deposit amounts is required by the documented workflows.

browser_navigate.reason: The agent must open the target application. The runner separately restricts direct navigation to the configured origin.

browser_navigate_back.description: Go back to the previous page in browser history.
browser_navigate_back.reason: Back navigation is an ordinary browser action that may be needed to recover from a wrong path.

browser_network_requests.description: List network requests made since the page loaded.
browser_network_requests.reason: Network inspection exposes non-visible implementation details and could encourage API-level automation instead of UI interaction.

browser_network_request.description: Return headers or body details for one recorded network request.
browser_network_request.reason: Reading request headers or bodies can expose sensitive technical data and bypass the user-visible interface.

browser_run_code_unsafe.description: Run an arbitrary Playwright JavaScript snippet in the MCP server process.
browser_run_code_unsafe.reason: This tool is explicitly RCE-equivalent and allows arbitrary code in the Playwright server process; no target scenario justifies that authority.

browser_take_screenshot.description: Capture an image of the current page.
browser_take_screenshot.reason: Screenshots provide visual evidence and can help when accessibility snapshots omit important presentation details.

browser_snapshot.description: Capture the structured accessibility representation of the current page.
browser_snapshot.reason: Accessibility snapshots are the primary structured observation used to understand and verify the visible page.

browser_click.reason: Links and buttons drive every documented workflow. Final-submission clicks are separately gated by scenario authorization.

browser_drag.description: Drag from one visible page element to another.
browser_drag.reason: Dragging between visible elements is a normal UI actuator and is safe to leave available even though the current target may not need it.

browser_hover.description: Hover over a visible page element.
browser_hover.reason: Hovering may reveal otherwise hidden UI information without accessing application internals.

browser_select_option.description: Select one or more options in a dropdown.
browser_select_option.reason: Product and statement choices use dropdown or selection controls in the account-opening workflow.

browser_tabs.description: List, create, close, or select a browser tab.
browser_tabs.reason: Tab selection is a normal browser operation that may be needed if a workflow opens a new page; new-tab URLs remain origin-restricted.

browser_wait_for.description: Wait for text, disappearance, or a specified duration.
browser_wait_for.reason: Explicit waiting may be required for redirects, transient screens, or delayed UI state. Repeated runs will show whether it is actually needed.
